correctness.rationale: Checked the argument in RESULT.md lines 19–53. Digit-sum parity gives the containing families (1,d,1), (0,1,d), (d,1,0) for length-four differences. Reversing a factor reverses and negates its differences. The image of the first family has both outer entries −1 and misses all three families; the other images have middle entry −1 and at least one outer entry 0 and also miss all three. This uses only 1≠−1 mod ell (and −1≠0), so applies at ell=3 and 4 as well as all larger moduli. At any greater length a putative reversal would give a forbidden length-four pair. For length three both a difference pair and its negated reversal must contain 1; only (1,−1) and (−1,1) satisfy both, giving palindromes. The disjoint binary blocks in m=2^(k+1)(2^r−1)+2^k−1 give s_2(m)=r+k and s_2(m+1)=r+1, including k=0 or r=0, so arbitrary ordered pairs are realized using the stated congruences. Applying the even/odd rules to all pairs gives the two families of ell² triples whose intersection has ell, and exactly 2ell length-three palindromes. The two-letter reversal orbits give ell(ell+1)/2; the one-letter and empty counts follow. The proof establishes the infinite claims; an independent prefix check for moduli 3,4,5 and first 4096 terms merely corroborates the short counts. VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected but not executed.

originality.rationale: There is exact coverage in the available index. Resultary f12270a0ea48 treats arbitrary base b and states the sharp cutoff, length-three palindrome classification and reflection identity in its gcd(b−1,m)=1 or 2 branch. At b=2 the gcd equals 1 for every modulus. Resultary 4c1615f0a563 explicitly treats the identical binary-base word, including the exact length-three count. No theorem here survives those comparisons as a distinct finding. This is a statement-coverage conclusion, not a determination of publication priority. Allouche et al.'s Question 62 is an open question with an observed pattern, not a formal all-moduli conjecture.
